newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian state-run banks seen following SBI rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Indian state-run banks seen following SBI rate cut.

text.p: The banking industry is set for a round of cuts in prime lending rates by state-run banks following the decision by the State Bank of India (SBI) to cut its prime lending rate, bankers said on Thursday.
Earlier, SBI had announced a cut in its prime lending rate to 15.5 percent per annum (exclusive of interest tax) from 16 percent. The revised rate takes effect from September 6.
"SBI is the industry leader," an official at a Bombay-based state-run bank said. "We will have to follow suit if we are to retain our customers."
"For all practical purposes, the remaining state-run banks are likely to announce cuts similar to SBI in the next few days," another banker said.
"In principle, the decisions have already been taken. Only the formality of approval from the respective boards of directors remains before the new rates are announced."
Banking analysts had been expecting a cut in lending rates aimed at reviving demand for bank credit.

Demand for bank credit has shown a negative growth in financial 1996/97 (April-March) with total advances by commercial banks in India at 2,687.05 billion rupees as on August 16, 1996, a fall of 18.02 billions from the March 29 figure.
Bank credit grew by 2.92 billion rupees during the same period last year, according to data published by the Reserve Bank of India.
